about: Which UK public body manages the UK's relationship with each international body, trading bloc or treaty organisation, or is its single point of contact. Each row cites an official page that says so, read 22 November 2026. Roles, never people. 'way_in' is the UK mission or delegation where there is one; 'lead' is the UK body that holds the relationship.

groups.assoc: The Commonwealth and other associations of states

bodies.name: European Union
bodies.way_in: UK Mission to the European Union (Brussels)
bodies.role: The Cabinet Office holds overall responsibility for the UK's relationship with the EU; a Cabinet Office minister co-chaired the Trade and Cooperation Agreement Partnership Council and the Withdrawal Agreement Joint Committee in February 2026. Since July 2026 a joint Cabinet Office and Foreign Office Minister of State holds EU policy and relations. The Foreign Office runs the mission in Brussels.

evidence.title: GOV.UK: Minister of State (Minister for Intergovernmental Relations and European Relations)
GOV.UK: Joint statement on the Joint Committee and Partnership Council meetings, 2 February 2026
GOV.UK: UK Mission to the European Union

bodies.name: World Trade Organization
bodies.way_in: UK Mission to the WTO, UN and other international organisations (Geneva)
bodies.role: Trade policy at the WTO was led by the Department for Business and Trade, now part of the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade (from 9 November 2026). The Foreign Office runs the Geneva mission.

evidence.title: GOV.UK: Minister of State for Trade Policy (WTO, G7, G20, OECD, Commonwealth engagement)
GOV.UK API: Department for Business and Trade, closed 9 November 2026 and superseded
GOV.UK: UK Mission to the WTO, UN and other international organisations (Geneva)

bodies.name: Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP)
bodies.role: The Department for Business and Trade negotiated and holds UK membership; its work passed to the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade on 9 November 2026.

evidence.title: Department for Business and Trade: draft explanatory memorandum on the UK's accession to CPTPP
GOV.UK API: Department for Business and Trade, closed 9 November 2026 and superseded
